q: What Cobb angle usually warrants surgical correction?
why: Over 40° is severe and usually needs surgery; cardiorespiratory compromise increases beyond about 65–100°.

q: What type of lung defect does severe scoliosis cause?
why: Restrictive lung disease, progressing to respiratory failure, pulmonary hypertension and RV failure in severe curves.

q: What is the commonest cause of scoliosis?
During scoliosis correction, MEPs are lost after rod distraction. BP and temperature are normal. What should happen?
o: Tell the surgeon, check physiology, and consider releasing the correction or a wake-up test
why: A focal signal loss after a surgical step suggests cord injury: reverse the manoeuvre, optimise MAP and consider a wake-up test.

q: What has neuromonitoring done to the risk of cord injury in scoliosis surgery?
why: IONM has reduced the risk of spinal cord injury from about 5% to 0.5%.

q: Which neuromuscular disease causing scoliosis is associated with cardiomyopathy?
why: Duchenne muscular dystrophy causes cardiomyopathy; assess with echo before surgery.

q: The ETT is dislodged while the patient is prone. What is the immediate management?
o: Turn the patient supine immediately before anything else
Call for help, insert an LMA to oxygenate, then intubate through it with a fibreoptic scope if needed
Bag-mask ventilation in the prone position for the rest of the case
Wait for the case to end
why: Call for help; an LMA can be placed prone to restore oxygenation, then a tube passed over a fibreoptic scope.

q: What is the inheritance of myotonic dystrophy?
why: Autosomal dominant; myotonia, distal weakness, cardiac conduction defects, cataracts and frontal balding.

q: Which drug can trigger myotonic contractures in myotonic dystrophy?
why: Triggers include neostigmine, cold, shivering, pain and stimulation; patients are sensitive to sedatives.

q: In Lambert–Eaton myasthenic syndrome, what happens to strength with repeated effort?
why: Antibodies to presynaptic calcium channels; repeated stimulation increases calcium and ACh release, so strength briefly improves. Often paraneoplastic (small cell lung cancer).
